record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: For a compact 3-manifold M and conformal data (gamma_ab, A_cd, tau) used in the Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York system, where gamma_ab is a Riemannian metric, A_cd is traceless, divergence-free, and symmetric, and tau is the mean curvature, what conditions guarantee solvability when tau is not constant?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact 3-manifold without boundary. Consider the following conformal data on $M$:
- a Riemannian metric $\gamma_{ab}$,
- a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor $A_{cd}$ that is traceless ($\gamma^{cd}A_{cd}=0$) and transverse (divergence-free, $\nabla^c A_{cd}=0$) with respect to $\gamma_{ab}$,
- a smooth scalar function $\tau$ on $M$ (the prescribed mean curvature).

The Lichnerowicz–Choquet-Bruhat–York (LCBY) system for an unknown positive conformal factor $\varphi>0$ and an unknown vector field $W^a$ on $M$ is:
$$\Delta_\gamma \varphi \;=\; \tfrac{1}{8} R(\gamma)\,\varphi \;-\; \tfrac{1}{8}\,\bigl|A + \mathbb{L}W\bigr|_\gamma^{2}\,\varphi^{-7} \;+\; \tfrac{1}{12}\,\tau^{2}\,\varphi^{5},$$
$$\nabla^{b}\!\bigl(\mathbb{L}W\bigr)_{ab} \;=\; \tfrac{2}{3}\,\varphi^{6}\,\nabla_{a}\tau,$$
where $(\mathbb{L}W)_{ab} = \nabla_a W_b + \nabla_b W_a - \tfrac{2}{3}\gamma_{ab}\nabla_c W^c$ is the conformal Killing operator and $R(\gamma)$ is the scalar curvature of $\gamma_{ab}$.

Solving the LCBY system produces an initial data set $(\bar\gamma_{ab},\bar K_{ab})=(\varphi^{4}\gamma_{ab},\, \varphi^{-2}(A+\mathbb{L}W)_{ab} + \tfrac{1}{3}\tau\varphi^{4}\gamma_{ab})$ for the vacuum Einstein constraint equations on $M$.

Problem. Determine general conditions on the conformal data $(\gamma_{ab}, A_{cd}, \tau)$, with $\tau$ not constant on $M$, which guarantee that the LCBY system admits a solution $(\varphi, W)$ with $\varphi>0$. In particular, identify a sharp class of non-CMC data extending the known constant-$\tau$ existence theory (e.g., generalizing it so as to apply whenever $|\nabla \log \tau|$ is sufficiently small, and beyond).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of solvability of the LCBY (conformal) constraint equations for non-constant mean curvature $\tau$ on closed 3-manifolds remains only partially solved. The constant-mean-curvature case was fully classified by Isenberg (1995). For non-CMC data, existence results have been obtained in the near-CMC regime by Isenberg–Moncrief and others, and in the far-from-CMC regime by Holst–Nagy–Tsogtgerel (2009) and Maxwell (2009) under smallness assumptions on the freely specified data; Maxwell also produced non-existence and non-uniqueness counterexamples for far-from-CMC data. A fully general criterion characterizing solvability for arbitrary non-constant $\tau$ is still not known.

status_evidence.title: Rough solutions of the Einstein constraint equations with nonconstant mean curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for the conformal constraint equations with nonconstant mean curvature using fixed-point/limit-equation arguments.
status_evidence.claim: Partial existence results are available for non-CMC data, but only under restrictions (near-CMC or smallness of freely specifiable data).

status_evidence.title: A non-existence result for a generalization of the equations of the conformal method
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples and non-existence for far-from-CMC conformal constraint equations.
status_evidence.claim: There exist non-CMC conformal data for which the LCBY system has no solution, showing the problem is not fully solved.

status_evidence.title: A new approach towards the construction of initial data in general relativity with positive Yamabe invariant and arbitrary mean curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work attempting to extend existence theory for the conformal constraint equations to arbitrary mean curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Research is ongoing and the general non-CMC solvability question is still actively studied.
